method: Optional binary add-on: the reviewed ARM binary was reproduced from the project source tree, and every third-party component linked into it ships its required notice beside the binary

details.distribution: sdk/optional/weniclaw ships the stripped ARM FDPIC binary (253512 B, sha256 above), its README, notice texts and five peripheral skill texts under skills/; sdk/optional/install.sh installs WeniClaw and gpioctl through temporary files followed by atomic rename, then copies skills/ to /system/weniclaw/workspace/skills, where the agent reads them on demand. The port source and its build script are maintainer material and are not part of the published tree; the reviewed build inputs stay recorded in licenses/components.json build materials and this evidence. Zig build caches and output directories are local build state, excluded from the distribution inventory.
details.license: WeniClaw code is BSD-3-Clause, copyright 2026 Nsing Technologies Inc. The <think> block parser is independently implemented project code. No third-party parser source or license text is included.
details.linked_code: Built with Zig 0.16.0, whose runtime and bundled musl-derived Linux C declarations keep their own MIT and COPYRIGHT notices; both texts ship in sdk/optional/weniclaw/licenses/. The ARM executable dynamically links the rootfs libcurl and Mbed TLS shared objects (curl licence shipped as licenses/curl-COPYING.txt; Mbed TLS is taken under Apache-2.0, recorded by the mbedtls component). The WeChat text channel follows Tencent's published protocol documentation and is independently implemented; no Tencent plugin source or asset is included.
details.build: sdk/optional-src/weniclaw/build.sh host|arm, documented in sdk/optional-src/weniclaw/doc/build.md. The ARM build needs Zig 0.16.0, the SDK cross compiler, the public FDPIC libcurl.so.4 built with eventfd disabled, and the Mbed TLS headers; every input is either in this repository or a pinned upstream release.
details.upstream: WeniClaw is written for this project and is not a vendored upstream. Its own source, including the think-block parser, has no upstream source dependency; Zig, musl-derived declarations and libcurl remain separately identified dependencies.
details.task_api: The same wechat run process exposes a root-only HTTP/JSON control socket at /run/weniclaw/control.sock. It persists bounded tasks under /system/weniclaw/queue and supports delivery or one no-history, no-tool agent step before delivery. The implementation limits requests to 16 KiB, records to 32 KiB, storage to 32 records and 16 active tasks, execution to three attempts, pipelines to four steps and one agent step, and image artifacts to the configured workdir/media roots. These limits keep the API within the existing agent process rather than creating a second daemon or thread.
details.scheduled_tasks: Durable AI schedules use the existing wechat run thread and a one-second scan interval. Recurring schedules have a 30-second minimum. A scheduled run appends a control instruction to the stored prompt: when no notification is appropriate, the model must return exactly __WENICLAW_SILENT__; the scheduler then records successful completion without calling the WeChat send API. Exact matching avoids treating natural-language outcomes such as 'no hand' as notification control messages. Ordinary final text remains deliverable.
details.elf: ARM FDPIC (ET_DYN, OS/ABI ARM FDPIC, interpreter /lib/ld-uClibc.so.0); NEEDED libcurl.so.4, libmbedtls.so.21, libmbedx509.so.7, libmbedcrypto.so.16 and libc.so.0. The largest executable mapping is 241664 bytes; the dynamically loaded libcurl is 363524 bytes with a 346176-byte largest mapping, within the 512 KiB buddy-block budget. The stack upper bound is 131072 bytes.
